# PRACTICE DIRECTION 40D –

pd_part40e

# This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40] Contents of this Practice Direction

## PART 1 – COURT’S POWERS IN RELATION TO LAND

## Application to the court where land subject to an incumbrance

## 1.1

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.1] In this paragraph ‘incumbrance’ has the same meaning as it has in section 205(1) of the Law of Property Act 1925.

## 1.2

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.2] Where land subject to any incumbrance is sold or exchanged any party to the sale or exchange may apply to the court for a direction under section 50 of the Law of Property Act 1925 (discharge of incumbrances by the court on sales or exchanges).

## 1.3

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.3] The directions a court may give on such an application include a direction for the payment into court of a sum of money that the court considers sufficient to meet –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.3] (1) the value of the incumbrance; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.3] (2) further costs, expenses and interest that may become due on or in respect of the incumbrance.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.3] (Section 50(1) of the Law of Property Act 1925 contains provisions relating to the calculation of these amounts)

## 1.4

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.4] Where a payment into court has been made in accordance with a direction under section 50(1) the court may –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.4] (1) declare the land to be freed from the incumbrance; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.4] (2) make any order it considers appropriate for giving effect to an order made under rule 40.16 or relating to the money in court and the income thereof.

## 1.5

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.5] An application under section 50 should –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.5] (1) if made in existing proceedings, be made in accordance with CPR Part 23;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 1.5] (2) otherwise, be made by claim form under CPR Part 8.

## Directions about the sale etc.

## 2.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] Where the court has made an order under rule 40.16 it may give any other directions it considers appropriate for giving effect to the order. In particular the court may give directions –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (1) appointing a party or other person to conduct the sale;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (2) for obtaining evidence of the value of the land;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (3) as to the manner of sale;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (4) settling the particulars and conditions of the sale;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (5) fixing a minimum or reserve price;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (6) as to the fees and expenses to be allowed to an auctioneer or estate agent;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (7) for the purchase money to be paid

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (a) into court;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (b) to trustees; or

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (c) to any other person;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (8) for the result of a sale to be certified;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 2.] (9) under rule 40.18.

## Application for permission to bid

## 3.1

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 3.1] Where –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 3.1] (1) the court has made an order under rule 40.16 for land to be sold; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 3.1] (2) a party wishes to bid for the land,

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 3.1] he should apply to the court for permission to do so.

## 3.2

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 3.2] An application for permission to bid must be made before the sale takes place.

## 3.3

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 3.3] If the court gives permission to all the parties to bid, it may appoint an independent person to conduct the sale.

## 3.4

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 3.4] ‘Bid’ in this paragraph includes submitting a tender or other offer to buy.

## Certifying sale result

## 4.1

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.1] If –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.1] (1) the court has directed the purchase money to be paid into court; or

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.1] (2) the court has directed that the result of the sale be certified,

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.1] the result of the sale must be certified by the person having conduct of the sale.

## 4.2

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.2] Unless the court directs otherwise, the certificate must give details of

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.2] (1) the amount of the purchase price;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.2] (2) the amount of the fees and expenses payable to any auctioneer or estate agent;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.2] (3) the amount of any other expenses of the sale;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.2] (4) the net amount received in respect of the sale;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.2] and must be verified by a statement of truth in the form set out in paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 22.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.2] (Part 22 sets out requirements about statements of truth)

## 4.3

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.3] The certificate must be filed

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.3] (1) if the proceedings are being dealt with in the Royal Courts of Justice, in Chancery Chambers;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 4.3] (2) if the proceedings are being dealt with anywhere else, in the court where the proceedings are being dealt with.

## Fees and expenses of auctioneers and estate agents

## 5.1

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.1] (1) Where the court has ordered the sale of land under rule 40.16, auctioneer’s and estate agent’s charges may, unless the court orders otherwise, include

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.1] (a) commission;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.1] (b) fees for valuation of the land;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.1] (c) charges for advertising the land;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.1] (d) other expenses and disbursements but not charges for surveys.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.1] (2) The court’s authorisation is required for charges relating to surveys.

## 5.2

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.2] If the total amount of the auctioneer’s and estate agent’s charges authorised under paragraph 5.1(1)

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.2] (1) does not exceed 2.5% of the sale price; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.2] (2) does not exceed the rate of commission that that agent would normally charge on a sole agency basis

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.2] the charges may, unless the court orders otherwise and subject to paragraph 5.3(3) and (4), be met by deduction of the amount of the charges from the proceeds of sale without the need for any further authorisation from the court.

## 5.3

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.3] If –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.3] (1) a charge made by an auctioneer or estate agent (whether in respect of fees or expenses or both) is not authorised under paragraph 5.1(1);

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.3] (2) the total amount of the charges so authorised exceeds the limits set out in paragraph 5.2;

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.3] (3) the land is sold in lots or by valuation; or

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.3] (4) the sale is of investment property, business property or farm property

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.3] an application must be made to the court for approval of the fees and expenses to be allowed.

## 5.4

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 5.4] An application under paragraph 5.3 may be made by any party or, if he is not a party, by the person having conduct of the sale, and may be made either before or after the sale has taken place.

## PART 2 – CONVEYANCING COUNSEL OF THE COURT

## Reference to conveyancing counsel

## 6.1

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.1] When the court refers a matter under rule 40.18, the court may specify a particular conveyancing counsel.

## 6.2

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.2] If the court does not specify a particular conveyancing counsel, references will be distributed among conveyancing counsel in accordance with arrangements made by the Chief Chancery Master.

## 6.3

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.3] Notice of every reference under rule 40.18 must be given to the Chief Chancery Master.

## 6.4

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.4] The court will send a copy of the order, together with all other necessary documents, to conveyancing counsel.

## 6.5

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.5] A court order sent to conveyancing counsel under paragraph 6.4 will be sufficient authority for him to prepare his report or draft the document.

## 6.6

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.6] (1) An objection under rule 40.19 to a report on title prepared by conveyancing counsel must be made by application notice.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.6] (2) The application notice must state –

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.6] (a) the matters the applicant objects to; and

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.6] (b) the reason for the objection.

[This practice direction supplements CPR Part 40 > 6.6] Updated: Sunday, 1 October 2023
